subject: review records and review identities of the programme (planeon.review-record/v2, planeon.review-identity/v2) as inputs to H-09 and H-32
purpose: R13 issue 1, recommendation 4: the fields a review-record series needs so that review independence, error detection and later refutation can be measured; a design input to REVIEW-RECORD-SERIES-001's 'decide accept or forbid' step (VIS-R13-I1-RL item 3). Denominators are defined here, before any collection.

fields.name: findingId
fields.definition: a stable identity of one finding across rounds: either an id that does not embed the raising round, or an id plus a 'supersedes' reference to the earlier id it carries forward (RL-02-PROPOSAL part 1)

fields.name: reviewedHead
fields.definition: the exact head (40-hex) the round reviewed; a finding is bound to that head

fields.name: round
fields.definition: the round number inside the series

fields.name: firstDetectionRound
fields.definition: the round in which the finding's identity first appeared (derived from findingId and round)

fields.name: recurrence
fields.definition: the number of later rounds that raise the same findingId again (a re-raise)

fields.name: severity
fields.definition: the finding's severity as the record form fixes it

fields.name: blocks
fields.definition: whether the finding blocks the verdict

fields.name: disposition
fields.definition: the author's disposition of the finding in the next round (addressed, disputed, deferred, rejected) with a note

fields.name: laterAdjudication
fields.definition: what later evidence said about the finding or the claim it disputed: confirmed, refuted or untested, by a later round, the verifier or the oracle, with the record that says so

fields.name: unanimity
fields.definition: whether every reviewer of the round accepted the claim (derived when a round has more than one reviewer record)
candidates: derived from verdict across reviewer records of one round

fields.name: verifierOutcome
fields.definition: the verifier's conclusion for the reviewed head after PASS_FOR_PUSH (success, failure, refused) with the check-run reference

fields.name: oracleContribution
fields.definition: the oracle's per-packet verdict and test count, with the oracle's sha256 and the placer identity digest, obtained from the merge-decision record's oracle block, never by reading protected tests

fields.name: reviewEffort
fields.definition: the effort of the round: the reviewer's runs and limits (review identity runs[]), launched and finished timestamps, and the author's minutes to address

fields.name: custodySeparation
fields.definition: whether the reviewer ran under a custodian separate from the author (operator role and agent id differ from the author's agent ids)

fields.name: contextSeparation
fields.definition: whether the reviewer held only the brief, the rules and the export (brief, rules and wrapper digests present; no shared transcript)

fields.name: modelFamily
fields.definition: the reviewer's model, recorded apart from custody and context so the three are never conflated

fields.name: interruptions
fields.definition: identity interruptions as strings (a 429 stop, a resume), so review effort and independence can be read against them

denominators.findings: findings[] entries across the series' rounds, de-duplicated by findingId
denominators.packets: merge-decision records with a merge commit
denominators.PASS_FOR_PUSH heads: heads a round marked PASS_FOR_PUSH, matched to a verifier run
denominators.claims per round: claims the round's verdict accepted or disputed

rules: the oracle side is read only through the custodian's summary (the oracle block); the lab never reads protected tests
every field is recorded, never inferred from prose, before the series' first collection
custody, context and model family are three fields, never one
